mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue to drift upward from their current depressed levels, weekday commuting and nearby discretionary stops will expand, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks versus the prior four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days despite a sustained rise in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in GROCERY_PHARM after an unusually weak week signals restored routine out-of-home errand behavior, which spills into more retail visits within one to two weeks and lifts RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM turns positive after at least 2 consecutive negative weekly means
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays below its prior 4-week average for the next 14 days after GROCERY_PHARM crosses from negative to positive.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL remains elevated while WORKPLACES falls further, people substitute toward at-home time and reduce discretionary shopping trips, causing RETAIL_REC to decline over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above +10 while WORKPLACES falls below -10
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises relative to its last 28-day mean even though RESIDENTIAL remains above +10 and WORKPLACES remains below -10.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in PARKS mobility captures fair-weather leisure substitution that draws trips away from malls and shopping streets, lowering RETAIL_REC within one week if the park surge persists.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 7 days after a >5-point rise in PARKS.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT recovers while WORKPLACES remains weak, commuting becomes less efficient for retail trips and the retail rebound stalls; RETAIL_REC will stay flat or fall over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by at least 3 points while WORKPLACES remains below -8
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 4-week mean during a period when TRANSIT improves but WORKPLACES stays below -8.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed rise in GROCERY_PHARM alongside falling RESIDENTIAL means more errands are being completed outside the home, and that shopping habit carries over into retail recreation, raising RETAIL_REC over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM increases while RESIDENTIAL declines from the prior week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase within 14 days after GROCERY_PHARM rises and RESIDENTIAL falls.

mechanism_narrative: A continued increase in WORKPLACES after a multiweek trough marks normalization of weekday circulation, and that broadens lunch and after-work retail trips, lifting RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises for 2 consecutive weeks after being below -8
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not outperform its prior 28-day average over the next month after WORKPLACES rises for two straight weeks from below -8.

mechanism_narrative: If both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES worsen together, the city is likely entering a mobility contraction that suppresses discretionary trips; retail and recreation should weaken within one week and remain below the recent average.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall by at least 2 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the week after simultaneous week-on-week declines in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.
